scope.summary: Implement BodyKit CRDT semantics per Section 13.27: channel edits as CRDT ops with LWW per channel id, competing whole-body proposals held as separate drafts (never silently merged), and the ai_edit_proposal lane carrying attributed model proposals — the concurrency substrate under edit_body and the GUI sliders.
acceptance_criteria: Every channel edit encodes as a CRDT op (channel id, value, lamport/hlc ordering, session attribution); LWW resolves per channel id, so concurrent edits to DIFFERENT channels always both land.
Concurrent edits to the SAME channel resolve LWW deterministically with both ops retained in the ledger (the losing op is auditable, not lost).
Competing whole-body proposals (two models proposing different bodies for one intent) exist as separate drafts with no auto-merge; promotion selects one explicitly.
The ai_edit_proposal lane wraps model-originated edits with proposal metadata (proposing session, rationale ref) consistent with the kernel-wide proposal pattern.
Replaying the op log from the ledger reconstructs the exact channel state (property test over randomized op interleavings).
scope.risk_if_missed: Parallel sessions clobber each other's channel edits or fork unmergeable state — the swarm-authoring proof (MT-607) and the GUI/model coexistence story both collapse without this substrate.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
